property_summary: Only the current owner should be able to change the owner via transferOwnership; the bug removes the ownership check, letting anyone change the owner.

A successful call to transferOwnership must revert when the caller is not the current owner; the bug allows non-owners to succeed, so after a non-owner call, the owner stays unchanged in the reference but changes in the mutant.
After any sequence of calls to transferOwnership, the owner can only change when msg.sender is the current owner; the bug removes the check, letting a non-owner change it.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership in the reference contract, the owner remains unchanged, but the buggy contract allows the non-owner to change the owner to a new address.
Only the current owner can change the owner address; the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
After a call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner state variable must equal the passed newOwner address; the buggy version instead sets it to address(0), violating this invariant.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership, the owner must equal the passed argument (correct) but the bug sets it to address(0), so for any input where newOwner != address(0) the property is violated.

After the owner successfully calls transferOwnership, no subsequent call by any account should ever cause a revert due to the onlyOwner modifier – because the owner always exists; the bug sets the owner to zero, so the modifier rejects every future onlyOwner action.

After any successful call to transferOwnership that changes the owner, the new owner must match the parameter that was passed; the bug sets the owner to address(0) regardless of the input, so the rule fails for any non-zero newOwner.
In the correct version, only the owner can call owned() without reverting; the buggy version allows anyone to call owned() without reverting, violating the access control invariant.
For every address, a non-owner call to owned() must revert; the bug allows such calls to succeed.
For any address, if the caller is not the owner then owned() must revert; the bug removes the owner check so non-owner calls succeed.

For any `msg.sender` that is not the `owner`, calling `owned()` must revert in the reference contract; the bug bypasses the onlyOwner guard so `owned()` succeeds for any sender, violating the access control.
